subject: MAP Kickstart — Dedicated GPU throughput & owner roster
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wright <sam.wright@aperturelabs.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP Kickstart — Dedicated GPU throughput & owner roster

Sam / team — thanks again for taking the pilot conversations forward. Per our call last week I wanted to kick off a short MAP (mutual action plan) scoped to Dedicated capacity for your inference workloads so we align on roles, throughput targets, and a close timeline.

Attachments: MAP_Dedicated_v0.1.xlsx (MAP draft), capacity_workbook_aperture.csv (initial numbers), throughput_targets_p95.png (visual).

Goal: get a production-ready Dedicated pool scoped and priced so Aperture can start a volume pilot in Jan 2027 with a target GA decision by end of Q1 2027. Proposed close timeline: pilot agreement signed by 2026-12-20, pilot onboarded by 2027-01-15, GA decision by 2027-03-31.

Quick asks / next actions:
- Please review the attached MAP draft and fill in your internal approvers in column B (procurement/legal).
- Sam: confirm the sustained throughput target (tokens/sec) and typical sequence lengths for the top 2 models. I put placeholder numbers in the capacity workbook.
- Marissa (PM): own the MAP delivery and weekly sync.
- Rishi (SE): lead the capacity scoping and initial performance evals.
- Lauren (CS): define success metrics (latency, p95, error budget) and onboarding checkpoints.

Proposed cadence: 30-minute weekly sync (Tuesdays 10:00 PT) + an initial 60-minute kickoff this Thursday 11/10 at 10:00 PT. If that works I will send a calendar invite and HubSpot update.

Thanks — looking forward to a compact plan.

— Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Sam Wright <sam.wright@aperturelabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aperturelabs.com
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MAP Kickstart — Dedicated GPU throughput & owner roster

Sergio — thanks, this looks good as a start. A few clarifications from our side:

- Aperture's primary constraint is steady inference for our recommendation model (Model-A). We're aiming for ~350k tokens/min sustained across the fleet (estimate in your sheet assumed 250k). Burst tolerance up to 500k for short windows.
- Typical sequence length: 128 tokens for recommendations; 512 for analytics queries (heavy tails, <10% of requests).
- We will need KMS integration and support for VPC peering during pilot (security requirement).
- Procurement copied above; they will need the commercial MAP and basic SOW to start review.

I can confirm Thursday 11/10 at 10:00 PT for the kickoff. I'll bring our infra lead if needed. I'll push the capacity numbers into your workbook tonight.

— Sam
Sam Wright, VP Product — Aperture Labs
sam.wright@aperturelabs.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Sam Wright <sam.wright@aperturelabs.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 12:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP Kickstart — Dedicated GPU throughput & owner roster

Thanks — added a technical tab in capacity_workbook_aperture.csv with an initial memory / kv-cache estimate. A few notes from the SE side:

- For 350k tokens/min sustained we should consider a mix of p4d-style instances and quantized LLMs (int8) to control cost. I sketched two cluster options in the workbook (balanced / performance-first).
- Need a representative request trace (1k requests) with sequence length distribution and top-k/top-p sampling settings to run a realistic throughput run. If Aperture can share a sanitized sample, we can run a dry-run on our dedicated staging pool.
- Can we get clarity on whether cold-start latency budget is 200ms (typical) or stricter? That affects batching and pool sizing.

I attached a short checklist to the MAP (under the technical tab). I'll own the first throughput run and can have results within 7 business days of getting the trace.

— Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Sam Wright <sam.wright@aperturelabs.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP Kickstart — MAP Kickstart — Dedicated GPU throughput & owner roster

Looping in onboarding considerations from CS:

- Success metrics (suggested): p95 latency < 150ms for recommendation paths, error rate < 0.5%, rollout completion within 4 weeks of pilot start.
- Compliance asks: please confirm SOC 2 report possession and whether KMS will be customer-managed. I added a checklist item in the MAP draft for docs we need to hand to procurement.
- Marissa: can you add a separate column in the MAP for "procurement owner" and target review dates so we don't get blocked?

Link to the shared kickoff notes: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cMAPDraft (I added the onboarding section). I've also created a HubSpot activity (HS-1249876) and assigned the initial task for legal review.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP Kickstart — Dedicated GPU throughput & owner roster

Perfect — thanks all for the quick replies. Summary / immediate next steps:

1) Sam to update capacity_workbook_aperture.csv with Aperture's trace + confirm KMS/VPC ask (target: tonight).
2) Rishi to run initial sizing after receiving trace (target: results by 11/17).
3) Marissa to publish updated MAP with procurement owners and schedule weekly sync (first sync 11/16).
4) Lauren to attach SOC2 summary and procurement checklist to the MAP (for procurement review).
5) Sergio to issue kickoff invite for 11/10 10:00 PT and push HubSpot deal stage to "MAP initiated".

I'll send the invite now. If anything urgent comes up procurement@aperturelabs.com please copy me.

Cheers —
